column1: # Things the archive MUST be able to answer, checked against the live database.
# ⚠ **THESE ARE POSITIVE CONTROLS, NOT COVERAGE.** On 2026-09-18 four separate
# absences were reported that the checking method had manufactured: Google Chat
# "had no replies" (126 existed), the capture was "clean" (it took no
# attachments at all), Signal "had no read state" (receipts had been discarded
# for fifteen months), formatting affected "28,000 messages" (1,145). Each null
# came from a check that could not have produced a positive, and each was
# written as a fact about the service rather than about the measurement.
# A row here is an instance Pippijn KNOWS is true, independent of this archive.
# If the query stops returning it, the pipeline has lost something — and unlike
# an audit, that failure announces itself. Silence from a check that has never
# been shown to detect anything is worth nothing.
# ⚠ **A ROW MUST BE TRUE NOW, NOT EXPECTED TO BECOME TRUE.** The first version of
# this file asserted that some message carried both a delivery AND a read
# receipt — plausible, and false: receipt capture had started hours earlier and
# no message had both yet. It reported LOST on a pipeline that had lost nothing.
# A control that fails for a reason other than loss teaches the reader to ignore
# it, which is how a check dies.
# ⚠ **DO NOT GENERATE ROWS FROM THE DATABASE.** A row derived from the archive
# tests that the archive agrees with itself, which is the exact failure above.
# Every row must come from somewhere else: his memory, his phone, the Chat UI.
# Run:  tools/check_known_truths.py
# Format: name <TAB> expected <TAB> sql
name
gchat: "Me too." answers the message about living long enough
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gchat_messages r JOIN gchat_messages t ON t.group_id=r.group_id AND t.msg_id=r.reply_to_msg_id WHERE r.msg_id='NUy91jT1Uwg' AND t.text LIKE 'I hope I%ll live long enough%'
